text:
maria: Heads up — nightly perf CI flagged a p99 token latency regression on master after the 03/17 merge.
ci-bot: Perf alert: job runtime/perf-e2e #482 exceeded threshold. baseline p99=280ms -> current p99=396ms. test=long-dialog-2k. build: nightly-2026-03-17. link: https://ci.redwood/investigate/482
kevin: Which merge did CI point to? any suspect range from the bisect data?
maria: CI traces show the delta introduced between abc1234..defa7c1 (those are example short hashes). Bisect hint in CI suggests the range includes batching changes.
raj: I reproduced locally: pulled nightly image redwood/runtime:nightly-2026-03-17, ran long-dialog-2k load with 16 connections. p99 matches CI.
raj: Quick local notes: when I force kernel selection to previous strategy (kernel_selector=v1) p99 drops back to ~285ms.
kevin: That smells like kernel selection interacting with new batching heuristics. Could be kernel choice made worse for longer contexts.
liz: I'll run git bisect on the runtime branch. Command I'm starting with:
```
cd services/runtime
git fetch origin
git checkout main
git bisect start defa7c1 abc1234
# test script returns 0=good, 1=bad
```
liz: ETA ~45m for a bisect run on my workstation (local perf harness).
oliver: If bisect narrows it to the batching heuristic commit, we should test reverting that commit in staging before a rollback in prod.
raj: Quick profiler dump from a bad build (cropped):
```
# perf top sample
25.8% kernel_selector::choose_kernel
18.3% batching::heuristic::compute_batch_boundaries
12.1% kvcache::lookup_miss_handler
 9.4% attention::attention_forward
```
raj: Notably, kvcache lookup miss rate increased ~8% in the bad build, which could amplify p99 on long-context workloads.
kevin: Huh. Increased KV misses could be from batch boundary changes causing more fragmented KV usage. That matches the heuristic change.
maria: Liz, any luck with bisect?
liz: Found the first bad commit: defa7c1 -> changes to adaptive batch smoothing + kernel choice fallback order. Bisect landed on commit defa7c1 exactly.
liz: Quick patch test: cherry-pick the revert of the smoothing lines and rerun.
raj: I applied the revert locally and re-ran long-dialog-2k. p99=292ms, matches pre-merge. CPU/GPU utilization roughly same, KV miss rate back to baseline.
kevin: Good. That gives us a clear regression vector. Plan: 1) open PR to revert smoothing lines (emergency), 2) add unit/integration test that simulates long-context KV patterns, 3) investigate smarter kernel fallback ordering.
maria: Agreed. Can we get a staged revert to unblock the rollout?
oliver: I'll open the emergency revert PR and request fast-track. tagging @eng-oncall.
ci-bot: Build #483 triggered for revert PR #521. Running perf e2e.
liz: After revert PR merged to staging, monitor perf e2e. If green, merge to main and cut a patch release.
kevin: Also postmortem action item: improve bisect automation to run a small perf harness during bisect so we can auto-detect these cases faster.
maria: Thanks team. I'll draft the incident note and list the root cause as "adaptive batch smoothing + kernel fallback order increased KV cache churn causing higher p99 for long-context generation."
raj: For follow-up: benchmark different smoothing alphas, measure KV locality, and add a KV-heavy synthetic test to our CI perf suite.
oliver: Will coordinate patch release timeline with product.
maria: Closing thread for now — continuing investigation in a follow-up thread once we have the deeper profiler results. :thumbsup:
